title: A Contact for the Cipher
premise: Oscar Winterbourne, a disgraced signals analyst haunted by the botched operation that ended his career, receives calls on an unregistered burner from Elena Vasquez — his former partner and lover, officially dead for two years. She's alive, embedded with the mercenary network planning to assassinate a foreign minister at the Geneva summit, and she needs Oscar to decrypt the cipher that will expose her cover before her handlers kill her. Torn between loyalty to the woman he loves and duty to the agencies that burned him, Oscar races to trade the decrypted cipher — the one secret worth killing for — to a blackmailed intelligence broker in exchange for Elena's extraction. At the summit's eve, Oscar chooses truth over both law and love: he broadcasts the cipher publicly, burning the network, saving Elena, and surrendering himself to justice outside any institution's control.
about_author: Petra Thornbury is a former diplomatic translator who spent a decade shuttling between embassies before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about people trapped between institutions and their consciences, drawing on the encrypted silences she witnessed in negotiation rooms.

chapters.title: The Number That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Insomniac and half-feral in a Lisbon safehouse flat, Oscar answers a burner phone left in his mailbox. The voice is Elena's — dead two years, buried by the same agencies that discarded him. She gives him thirty seconds of proof only she could know, then a fragment of cipher and a warning: they're watching him already. Emotional beat: dread curdling into desperate hope.

chapters.title: Dead Frequency
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Oscar decrypts the first cipher layer while evading surveillance; Elena, inside the mercenary cell in Geneva, plays the loyal operative while sabotaging the assassination timeline. Their parallel chapters braid together through the phone calls — love conducted in tradecraft. Oscar realizes the cipher contains the summit hit list. Emotional beat: intimacy rebuilt under threat.

chapters.title: The Price of the Key
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The agencies find him first — his old handler offers reinstatement if he hands over the cipher and lets Elena die as planned. Simultaneously, the network's fixer corners him with photographs of Elena's real fate if he talks. Squeezed between duty and love, Oscar cuts a third deal with a blackmailed broker: the full decryption for extraction. Emotional beat: betrayal on every side, resolve hardening.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Summit eve, dual POV converging. The broker double-crosses them; Elena's cover blows; Oscar realizes no secret trade can save her — only sunlight can. He uploads the entire cipher to open channels worldwide, detonating the network's legitimacy and forcing every agency to protect the summit rather than bury it. In the chaos, he reaches Elena. He surrenders to no one; they walk into the crowd. Emotional beat: catharsis — truth chosen over survival.
